root_cause.text: nci_close_device() holds req_lock while flushing rx_wq, but the rx work handler can take req_lock (via nci_request), creating a circular locking dependency.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "nci_close_device() flushes rx_wq and tx_wq while holding req_lock. This causes a circular locking dependency because nci_rx_work() running on rx_wq can end up taking req_lock too: nci_rx_work -> nci_rx_data_packet -> nci_data_exchange_complete -> __sk_destruct -> rawsock_destruct -> nfc_deactivate_target -> nci_deactivate_target -> nci_request -> mutex_lock(&ndev->req_lock)." The patch moves flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq) to after mutex_unlock(&ndev->req_lock).

candidates.rationale: This flush of the RX workqueue is performed while holding req_lock, creating a circular locking dependency because the RX work handler can also acquire req_lock via nci_request.
Similar to RX flush, this TX workqueue flush runs while req_lock is held. If the TX work handler also acquires req_lock, it contributes to the same deadlock scenario.
Flushing the command workqueue while holding req_lock is also potentially dangerous if command work can acquire req_lock, widening the locking cycle.
This unlock marks the end of the critical section where req_lock is held. It confirms that the preceding workqueue flushes occur under lock, which is the root cause.
The close callback is invoked while holding req_lock. If this operation triggers any work that tries to acquire req_lock (e.g., through nci_request), it could also participate in the deadlock.

Flushing the TX workqueue while holding req_lock poses a similar risk if the TX work handler also acquires req_lock, contributing to the same deadlock scenario.
Flushing the command workqueue while holding req_lock is potentially dangerous if command work can acquire req_lock, widening the locking cycle and increasing deadlock likelihood.
Invoking the close callback while holding req_lock may trigger work that acquires req_lock (e.g., through nci_request), participating in the same circular dependency.
